brief.topic: The Small Edge That Helps Water Climb

s01: Water can climb inside a narrow glass tube.
In the thinner tube, it can settle higher.
Come closer, keeping the reservoir level in view.
Water meets the glass around a circular rim.
Surface tension supplies an upward pull along that rim.
The raised water has weight, pulling downward.
Double the radius, and the rim is twice as long.
But the cross sectional area becomes four times as large.
At the same height, that means four times the water weight.
The wider column must settle lower to balance.
For the same liquid and contact angle, height is inversely proportional to radius.
Twice the radius gives half the rise.
This is an equilibrium model for narrow, clean tubes.
It does not explain the whole journey of water through a tree.
Now compare a tube with three times the radius.
Its rise is one third as high.
A small boundary can support a surprising column, because its edge and its interior grow differently.

scenes.narration:
Water can climb inside a narrow glass tube. In the thinner tube, it can settle higher.

Come closer, keeping the reservoir level in view. Water meets the glass around a circular rim. Surface tension supplies an upward pull along that rim. The raised water has weight, pulling downward.

Double the radius, and the rim is twice as long. But the cross sectional area becomes four times as large. At the same height, that means four times the water weight. The wider column must settle lower to balance.

For the same liquid and contact angle, height is inversely proportional to radius. Twice the radius gives half the rise. This is an equilibrium model for narrow, clean tubes. It does not explain the whole journey of water through a tree.

Now compare a tube with three times the radius. Its rise is one third as high. A small boundary can support a surprising column, because its edge and its interior grow differently.
